note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative; the rule text is the author's illustrative text, not a statement of any law. The hypothetical replay changes only the supplied circumstance and never shows an outcome.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional delivery: take A leaves the parcel on the porch bench; the take is rewound, the analyst moves the flag to the window sill and the same take replays (what if: on the window sill — hypothetical). Condition 2 of a fictional house notice is joined to the changed circumstance as a plain relation; outcome not supplied.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a fictional equipment return in which the base take leaves the box in the wall parcel box and the hypothetical replay leaves it on the bench below (a different pair of spots, the replay reaching lower rather than stopping earlier). Different courier, two-condition rule, two issues, an editorial note on the flag.

facts.title: Laptop return at Unit 4 (fictional)
events: Carries the laptop box to the front

rules.title: Office return note (fictional text)
conditions: at the place named in the note

issues: Which place does the note name?
Is the bench part of the front?
assumptions: The tenant's route is the same in both takes

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long title, events, rule text, circumstance descriptions, issues, assumptions and captions to exercise wrapping and bounded shrinking.

facts.title: Evening delivery of a parcel at number 9 of fictional Linden Street
events: A courier from a fictional delivery service arrives at the garden at 18:10
The courier carries parcel number 7 all the way up to the house front
The courier leaves the parcel there and steps back towards the garden
Nobody opens the door while the courier is at the house

rules.title: House notice number 2 of the residents' association (illustrative)
conditions: A parcel addressed to a resident of the house is left for that resident
at a place that was agreed in advance with the resident concerned
before seven o'clock in the evening of the delivery day

circumstance.label: The exact place where the courier finally leaves the parcel
circumstance.baseText: on the wooden bench under the porch roof
circumstance.altText: on the stone sill of the front window instead

issues: Was the stone window sill ever agreed with the resident as a place for parcels?
Does the porch bench count as the same place as the window sill?
assumptions: Every other event happens exactly as in the base run of the scene
The courier's route and timing are the same in both takes
